subject: Request: Data transfer assurance and DPA annex details
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@metatech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Metatech Privacy Team <privacy@metatech.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 09:14:00 +0100
Subject: Request: Data transfer assurance and DPA annex details

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is keen to move forward but we need more detail on cross-border safeguards before legal can sign off. Can you provide the following by EOD PT on Friday (2028-04-07)?

1) The current DPA annex text (redline against our standard) and a summary of any clauses you cannot accept.
2) Evidence of transfer safeguards used for EU->US processing (DPF/SCC mapping, runtime controls, routing policies).
3) A current subprocessor list and note on how you handle subprocessors for cached K/V data.
4) Retention rules and audit log retention periods for request/response traces and KV cache metadata.
5) SOC2/ISO artifacts or a pointer to the S2 evidence bundle — we need to reference a specific set for procurement.

If you can also flag any operational constraints (e.g., no access to raw request bodies in hosted mode, encryption at rest exceptions, or export controls) that would help speed review.

Appreciate a single package (zip) and a short cover email that maps each numbered ask to a short answer.

Regards,
Liam O'Connor
Lead Privacy Manager
Metatech Solutions

---
Note: attaching our preferred DPA annex in the follow-up email.
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@metatech.com>
Cc: Metatech Privacy Team <privacy@metatech.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 10:03:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Request: Data transfer assurance and DPA annex details

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. We can deliver the package by end-of-day PT Friday. High-level notes here and I'll attach the evidence bundle and redline in the package: 

- DPA annex: we will provide a redline (see attached) and flag two negotiation items: (i) liability cap language tied to usage tier, (ii) limited carve-out for aggregated telemetry used in model performance monitoring. Both items are standard for our enterprise deals and we can propose specific language.
- Transfers: we use DPF + SCCs where required; runtime routing can pin EU traffic to EU-only pools for Dedicated/Private customers. Hosted customers use DPF+SCCs with documented controls.
- Subprocessors: current list provided; cached KV is stored encrypted and only accessible via service account keys; we do not export raw request bodies to subprocessors.
- Retention: request/response traces retained 90 days by default (configurable), KV cache metadata retained per customer policy (default 30 days).
- SOC2: we'll include the latest SOC2 Type II coverage summary and an evidence index referencing the S2 bundle.

I'll coordinate with Legal and Security to include the explicit mappings you requested.

Attachments (will send consolidated zip): redlined_dpa_annex_v3.pdf; s2_evidence_bundle_20280405.zip; subprocessor_list_q12028.csv

Best,
Jordan Blake
Director, Product Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 11:12:00 +01:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: Data transfer assurance and DPA annex details — action items

Folks — forwarding Metatech's ask. Quick division of work: 

- Karthik: can you produce the DPF/SCC mapping and a short paragraph describing runtime routing options (EU-only pinning, fallback policies) by EOD Thursday (our time)? We need explicit controls (prefix caching, KV encryption, compartmentalization).
- Kimberly: please assemble the SOC2 evidence index and zip the items we can share; confirm if any documents are redacted for hosted customers. Also validate retention windows for traces/KV metadata.
- I'll draft the redline to their DPA annex (attach proposed language for the two negotiation points) and combine the package.

If anything looks sticky once you pull docs, escalate to Legal (cc'd on the working thread). Thanks.

Jordan

Date: Fri, 07 Apr 2028 16:02:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Request: Data transfer assurance and DPA annex details — package delivered

Hi Liam,

Please find our consolidated package attached and answers inline below. Attachment list: redlined_dpa_annex_v3.pdf; s2_evidence_bundle_20280405.zip; subprocessor_list_q12028.csv.

Summary answers (mapping to your numbered list):

1) DPA annex: redline attached. Negotiation items: (a) Liability cap — we propose a cap tied to 12 months of paid fees for the specific product tier; (b) Telemetry carve-out — we propose language that allows aggregated telemetry for model health without exposing raw customer data, with opt-out available for Dedicated/Private deployments.

2) Transfer safeguards: We rely on the DPF+SCCs for EU->US transfers under hosted mode. For Dedicated customers we support EU-only routing and region-pinning. Controls included: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, prefix/KV caching encryption, per-customer encryption keys (KMS integration available), and strict role-based access controls. Detailed mapping is in the attached DPF_mapping.pdf inside the S2 bundle.

3) Subprocessors: Current list attached (subprocessor_list_q12028.csv). Policy: subprocessors are engaged under contractual obligations consistent with our DPA; no subprocessors access raw unredacted request bodies in hosted mode. KV cache is encrypted; access requires service account credentials and audit logging.

4) Retention: Default request/response traces: 90 days (configurable to between 30–540 days on enterprise plans). KV cache metadata: default 30 days; cached tokens/kv items may be purged earlier based on TTL. Audit logs (access events): retained 365 days for enterprise accounts, 90 days for standard hosted accounts.

5) SOC2: S2 evidence bundle attached with index.csv listing the artifacts and the assertion scope. We do not attach raw audit reports in the bundle; we can arrange a secure read-only access session for your auditors if you need the full report.

Operational constraints: For hosted customers, Palo-alto style packet captures or raw body exports are not available; we can provide filtered traces and structured redactions. Backup exports are encrypted and stored in geo-redundant storage under vendor contracts listed in the subprocessor CSV.

Next steps: If you want a call to walk through the mapping and DPA redline, I'm available Monday 10–12 PT or Tuesday 14–17 PT.

Best regards,
Jordan Blake
Director, Product Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlined_dpa_annex_v3.pdf (redline v3), s2_evidence_bundle_20280405.zip (index + artifacts), subprocessor_list_q12028.csv (current as of 2028-04-05)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@metatech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Metatech Privacy Team <privacy@metatech.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Apr 2028 17:45:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Request: Data transfer assurance and DPA annex details — package delivered

Jordan,

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the thorough package — appreciate the level of detail. A couple quick clarifications before we route to legal: 

- For the telemetry carve-out, can you confirm whether the aggregated telemetry ever includes hashed or pseudo-identifiers that could be linked back to a customer host? If so, we need that explicitly excluded.
- On audit log retention for enterprise accounts (365 days): is that configurable per-account? Can we shorten it for the initial pilot?

We'd like to take you up on a walkthrough — Monday 10:30 PT works for the core privacy reviewers. Please send a calendar invite with a link.

Regards,
Liam
Lead Privacy Manager
Metatech Solutions
